headline: Multi-omics profiling nominates prognostic markers and therapy-response genes across…
label: Cancer Prognostic Biomarker Discovery
summary: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics is increasingly used to nominate prognostic and treatment-response markers in cancer.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational discovery of prognostic or therapy-response markers from public transcriptomic resources, most often combining bulk cohorts such as TCGA and GEO with single-cell profiles. Recurrent analytic elements include WGCNA, survival modeling such as random survival forests, pseudotime analysis, and drug-sensitivity inference using GDSC2. Solid tumors dominate, including gastric, hepatocellular, prostate, lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal, pancreatic, and cervical cancers. Several items extend beyond signature construction. The FABP5 study links a gene to NF-κB/PD-L1 signaling, the PLPP2 and PSAT1 studies address radiotherapy resistance and ferroptosis, and the CTHRC1, SPAG5, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma studies report functional validation. The LBP analysis integrates 278,337 transcriptomic profiles in liver cancer. What is new is mainly the breadth of candidate genes and the joint treatment of immune microenvironment and drug response, not a shared mechanism. The items do not establish a common pathway.
